category_title: Second-grade Hispanic students who rely on graphophonic cues but struggle with semantic monitoring
minimal_context: The student is reading the book Amelia Bedelia and the Baby aloud during a one-on-one tutoring session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start reading this book, Amelia Bedelia and the Baby.

STUDENT: Okay. I want to read it, but I don't think I know enough words.

TUTOR: Just try your best. Go ahead and read the sentence on this page.

STUDENT: Babies should have...

TUTOR: What is the last word in that sentence?

STUDENT: (Looks at the picture) ...bowls. Babies should have bowls.

options.A: Implement the 'Follow the CAR' strategy during the session: (1) Commenting and waiting, (2) Asking for participation and waiting, and (3) Responding by adding more.
options.B: Create mini-lessons working on word endings (-ed and -s), and embed a lesson about couldn't and shouldn't into the second RMA session.
options.C: Integrate multicultural picture books into the one-on-one tutoring sessions, particularly focusing on reading African American stories with the student.
options.D: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the characters, setting, or plot of the story.
